facts.text: The Janey Ensminger Act, named after a Marine family member, authorized medical care for those who lived at Camp Lejeune between 1957 and 1987.
A 2023 study found Parkinson’s disease rates were 70% higher among veterans stationed at Camp Lejeune than at Camp Pendleton, hinting at water‑related risks.
Tarawa Terrace residents are zoned to Tarawa Terrace Elementary for PK‑5, while all base families attend Brewster Middle and Lejeune High.
From 1953 to 1987, Marines and families at Camp Lejeune drank and bathed in water contaminated with toxicants up to 3,400 times above safety limits.
Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune spans 246 square miles, making it one of the largest U.S. military training facilities.
The base’s 14 miles of beaches were built for amphibious assault training and sit between the deep‑water ports of Wilmington and Morehead City.
